bill.title: An Act amending the act of June 3, 1937 (P.L.1333, No.320), known as the Pennsylvania Election Code, in county boards of elections, further providing for expenses of county boards and of primaries and elections to be paid by county, expenses of special elections and boards to be provided with offices; in voting by qualified absentee electors, further providing for date of application for absentee ballot and for voting by absentee electors; and, in voting by qualified mail-in electors, further providing for voting by mail-in electors.

action.description: Laid on the table (Pursuant to Senate Rule 9)

posted_text:
✉️ PA SB 599 — Pennsylvania Counties Get a Boost: New Rules for Absentee Voting

Pennsylvania counties will now receive funding to support their election boards and provide offices for primary and election events.

The bill clarifies procedures for absentee voters, outlining when and how electors can apply for absentee ballots and how those ballots must be delivered – by mail or in person – to county election boards.

Specifically, it details the process for authorized representatives to deliver ballots and allows county judges to direct sheriff’s deputies to deliver ballots to electors who are unable to appear at a polling place or designate a representative.

The bill also sets out the rules for marking and returning mail-in ballots, requiring them to be delivered by mail or hand-delivered to the county board of elections by 8:00 PM on election day.

Oct. 20, 2026: Laid on the table (Pursuant to Senate Rule 9).

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.palegis.us/legislation/bills/2025/sb599
